_meta.label: Malignant germ cell tumour

settings.label: Stage I–II, completely resected: surveillance vs adjuvant chemotherapy
Advanced or incompletely resected (II–IV): primary chemotherapy
Bulky / unresectable: neoadjuvant chemotherapy vs primary surgery

tiers.1: Not used: no randomised ovarian germ cell trial
tiers.2: Standard: randomised survival evidence in male germ cell tumours (⚠️ extrapolated) plus ovarian single-arm series
tiers.6: No randomised ovarian data: single-arm, registry, paediatric or male-extrapolated
tiers.7: Do not use: inferior or toxic without benefit

_meta.summary: There is no randomised trial in ovarian germ cell tumours. BEP is the standard because male germ cell trials showed survival losses when bleomycin or cisplatin was dropped (⚠️ extrapolated); everything else ranks on ovarian single-arm, paediatric or registry data, then on subtype, age and toxicity.
_meta.tier_reading: Tier 2 = BEP, carried by male GCT randomised trials (EP ×3 and carboplatin–etoposide–bleomycin both lost survival against BEP) and ovarian single-arm cure rates; the extrapolation is marked on the card. Tier 6 = ovarian single-arm, paediatric or registry evidence, or male salvage series. Tier 7 = regimens that were inferior (VAC, PVB, EP ×3), toxic without survival gain (high-dose PEB) or inactive (checkpoint inhibitors). Within a tier, subtype, age group, staging and markers decide (surveillance is favoured for dysgerminoma IA, immature teratoma grade 1 and children; chemotherapy for yolk sac and mixed tumours and after incomplete staging).
_meta.platinum_free_interval: Germ cell platinum sensitivity uses a 4–6 week threshold, not 6 months; the setting chooses it and the epithelial PFI rules are off.

regimens.name: Surveillance after complete surgical staging (AFP / β-hCG + imaging); platinum chemotherapy at relapse

tox_ref.note: No treatment; about half of non-dysgerminoma patients will need chemotherapy at relapse

os.median: Paediatric stage I non-dysgerminoma (AGCT0132): 4-yr EFS 52%, OS 96%, 11/12 relapses salvaged. Adult stage IA (Charing Cross): relapse 36% non-dysgerminoma, 22% dysgerminoma, disease-specific survival 93%. MITO-9 prospective: 1/31 relapse on surveillance. Paediatric immature teratoma (INT-0106): 4-yr EFS 97.7%, OS 100%

pfs.text: Relapse is the trade: 43–52% in paediatric non-dysgerminoma series, 3–36% in adult series; all AGCT0132 recurrences were AFP-positive

qualifiers: No randomised surveillance-vs-chemotherapy trial; surveillance trades relapse for chemotherapy avoided, and salvage preserves OS
Requires complete surgical staging and reliable marker / imaging follow-up

prefer_when.reason: Immature teratoma grade 1: no relapses (MaGIC pooled IT)
Immature teratoma: chemotherapy looks least useful (UK cohort relapse 33% with vs 15% without; MaGIC paediatric no reduction in relapse)
Dysgerminoma stage I: MITO-9 group A surveillance; relapses salvaged with BEP
Paediatric protocols (INT-0106, AGCT0132) use surveillance for completely resected stage I
Raised markers make relapse detectable early (all AGCT0132 recurrences AFP-positive)

risk_rules.reason: Yolk sac: omitting chemotherapy looks most costly (NCDB stage IA/IB YST 5-yr OS 92.7% with vs 79.6% without); YST was the only independent OS factor in MITO-9
Incomplete peritoneal staging was the only independent recurrence factor in MITO-9 (26% vs 8.6%); restage or treat

regimens.name: BEP ×3 (cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5, bleomycin 30 U weekly, q21d)

tox_ref.note: No severe pulmonary toxicity, no drug-related deaths; AML 1, lymphoma 1

os.median: GOG-078: 91/93 completely resected stage I–III non-dysgerminoma free of germ cell cancer; paediatric PEB ×4 (POG 9048): 6-yr OS stage I 95.1%, stage II 93.8%

pfs.text: GOG-078: 2 clinical recurrences of 93; paediatric PEB ×4 6-yr EFS stage I 95%, stage II 87.5%

qualifiers: NTUH template = MD Anderson 3-day BEP (Gershenson 1990: cisplatin 100 mg/m² D1, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin infusion D1–3), given q3w instead of q4w; etoposide 300 vs 500 mg/m² per cycle in the GOG/EORTC trials. MD Anderson: 25/26 sustained remission, mostly without gross residual; authors suggested 5-day etoposide for bulky non-dysgerminoma.
Late effects: bleomycin lung 6.8% (risk: GFR <80, cumulative >300,000 IU, age >40), ototoxicity, second cancers

prefer_when.reason: Yolk sac / mixed: NCDB OS 92.7% with vs 79.6% without adjuvant chemotherapy (uncontrolled)

risk_rules.reason: Immature teratoma: UK cohort relapse 33% with vs 15% without chemotherapy; no radiological response of IT to chemotherapy
Paediatric stage I protocols use surveillance; chemotherapy did not reduce relapse in the paediatric MaGIC IT cohort
Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity (label: dose-related, lower doses in combination)
Age >40 is a bleomycin-lung risk factor (note: 6.8% overall)
Bleomycin label: CrCl <50 mL/min → dose reduction (70% at 40–50 … 40% at 5–10); cisplatin nephrotoxicity
Cisplatin label: consider discontinuation for grade 3–4 neuropathy

regimens.name: VAC (vincristine, dactinomycin, cyclophosphamide) ≥10 courses

tox_ref.note: Dose-limiting toxicity 30%; severe paresthesias or motor loss 85%

os.median: Failure 15/54 (28%) after complete resection; pure YST 46%

exclude_default.reason: Superseded: 28% failure after complete resection (46% in pure YST) vs 2/93 with BEP ×3 (GOG-078)

regimens.name: BEP ×3–4 (cisplatin 20 mg/m² D1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–5, bleomycin 30 U weekly or 15 U/m² D1, q21d)

tox_ref.note: Male GCT: less sensory neuropathy and better QoL at 3 months with 3 cycles; paediatric PEB ×4: grade 3–4 neutropenia 23%

os.median: ⚠️ Male GCT RCTs: BEP ×3 vs EP ×3 3-yr OS 95% vs 86% (P=.01); BEP vs carboplatin–etoposide–bleomycin 3-yr survival 97% vs 90% (OS HR 2.65 for carboplatin); BEP ×3 = ×4 in good prognosis (2-yr OS 97.0% vs 97.1%). Ovarian: advanced dysgerminoma 19/20 disease-free (GOG 90); MD Anderson 25/26 sustained remission; adult stage IC–IV 10-yr CSS 83.2%

pfs.text: Adult ovarian stage IC–IV (international cohort): 10-yr PFS 82.8%, first-line CR 84.6%; male BEP ×3 vs ×4 2-yr PFS 90.4% vs 89.4%

qualifiers: Survival evidence is from male GCT randomised trials (⚠️ extrapolated); ovarian data are single-arm
Do not drop cycles or bleomycin: EP ×3 lost survival (male); compressed PEb ×3 missed its EFS target in children (89% vs 92%) — authors: do not reduce 4 → 3

NTUH template = MD Anderson 3-day BEP (Gershenson 1990: cisplatin 100 mg/m² D1, etoposide 100 mg/m² D1–3, bleomycin infusion D1–3), given q3w instead of q4w; etoposide 300 vs 500 mg/m² per cycle in the GOG/EORTC trials. MD Anderson: 25/26 sustained remission, mostly without gross residual; authors suggested 5-day etoposide for bulky non-dysgerminoma.
Prognosis worse with both AFP and β-hCG raised (OS HR 3.90), stage IV, non-dysgerminoma and age ≥40

risk_rules.reason: Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity; consider an alternative without bleomycin with the GCT team
Age >40 is a bleomycin-lung risk factor (note: bleomycin lung 6.8%)
Bleomycin label renal dose reduction (CrCl <50); cisplatin nephrotoxicity; GFR <80 is a bleomycin-lung risk factor
Cisplatin label: consider discontinuation for grade 3–4 neuropathy

qualifiers: Equipoise in children (AGCT1531 randomising, unreported); no adult-female data

prefer_when.reason: Paediatric equivalence (EFS 86% vs 86%) with less ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity

risk_rules.reason: ⚠️ Carboplatin was inferior to cisplatin in adult men (OS HR 2.65); no adult-female data
